source.title: Neural Scaling Laws for Boosted Jet Tagging
source.authors: M. Vigl; N. Hartman; M. Kagan; L. Heinrich

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Applies scaling-law measurements to boosted-jet classification rather than language-model pretraining, and reports results for loss scaling, compute allocation, repeated data, and input configurations.
record.gate_note: The study measures validation cross-entropy for its own Transformer models and fits scaling relations. Results cited from other studies, including the ParT benchmark and prior scaling-law studies, are not recorded as this paper's results.
record.test_reason: The study trains its own Transformer jet classifiers over a grid of model and dataset sizes. It fits Chinchilla-form power laws to validation cross-entropy, derives a compute-optimal split and studies repeated data. These are its own results on whether the power-law form holds outside text pretraining (V5) and on how exponents and the split depend on setup (V7).
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is essentially right. Additions: the authors stress that β stays roughly constant across inputs and that repetition mainly lowers B while roughly preserving β. They also suggest simulation fidelity may limit achievable performance.
record.recipe_differences: Measures supervised boosted-jet classification loss and fits model-size, dataset-size, and compute relations, rather than language-model pretraining loss. It additionally studies repeated data and particle-feature configurations.
record.method_sensitivity: Repeated-data training changes the loss-law normalization and produces saturation or overfitting; input features and particle multiplicity change the asymptotic loss and fitted normalization, while the reported data exponent remains approximately similar.

fits_no_version.finding: The overfitting threshold scales as N ∝ D^0.47: the minimum model size needed to overfit grows roughly as the square root of dataset size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under data repetition, the model size needed to reach the data-limited loss scales as a power of dataset size.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-entropy loss maps smoothly onto QCD background rejection. The ParT benchmark is matched at the 100M-jet scale.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task-specific physics metrics are predictable from classification loss via an empirical mapping.

record.problems: The study uses one public simulated jet dataset and a set-Transformer encoder; it does not establish generality across architectures or modalities. The compute-optimal allocation is reported symbolically without a numerical fitted allocation exponent. The paper itself says broader study across modalities is needed; its asymptotic-loss interpretation for repeated data assumes the stated loss form continues to hold for infinite model size.

untested.parts: Not tested: no language-model pretraining loss.
Not tested: fits are made jointly on the grid. Figs 5–6 project to 100B samples without validating those projections against larger runs.
No language-model compute-optimal allocation is tested. The jet-domain split is recorded under V5/V7.
Not tested: depth is fixed at 4 layers and only width (embedding dimension) varies; no shape comparison at fixed N.
Not tested: image/video, fine-tuning and transfer. Only supervised jet classification and repeated data are covered.
Not tested: no downstream tasks separate from the training task. The loss-to-rejection mapping is for the same classification task.

missing.what: QCD rejection at 50% top efficiency shows a different scaling exponent with 10 particles: the metric-level exponent depends on the input representation.
The Muennighoff et al. data-constrained parametrization could not fit the results, because loss rises after a few epochs. This is evidence that the choice of functional form matters.
The numerical compute-optimal allocation exponent is not stated but is derivable as a≈0.33 from Table 1.

record.verdict_notes: Single architecture (4-layer set Transformer, width-scaled) on one simulated dataset. The L∞ in Table 1 is constrained to the repeated-data fit. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Tests boosted-jet classifiers, not held-out pretraining loss of language models.
The paper fits its loss surface jointly to the tested grid; it does not report a test in which fits to small runs predict much larger language-model runs.
Tests the compute-optimal parameter/data allocation for boosted-jet classifiers, not language models; does not establish a general trend across model families or fitting setups.
Does not compare depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count. It varies input representation and particle multiplicity instead.
Tests boosted-jet classification and repeated-data training, not image/video models, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Reports jet-tagging metrics related to its classification loss and data scale, but not downstream-task performance of language models or transfer from pretraining loss.

Shows sensitivity to data repetition and input representation, but does not compare alternative parameter-count conventions or fitting methods, nor directly test why published language-model laws disagree.

rows.subject: Transformer encoder grid (joint fit across tested model and dataset sizes)
rows.size_stated: Varied by embedding dimension; individual parameter counts not stated for this fit.
rows.operation_detail: Jointly fit validation loss as a function of model size N and dataset size D to L∞ + A/N^α + B/D^β.

conditions.value: Full 21-feature set; up to 128 particles per jet

rows.note: The paper says the fitted form describes the validation-loss points across a grid spanning several orders of magnitude in model size and dataset size. L∞ was constrained to the value obtained in Section 3.2.
rows.check: The baseline can be filled in from the paper's own reference: Hoffmann α≈0.38, β≈0.28 (Table 1 caption). The fit is not fully free: L∞ is constrained to the Section 3.2 value, which is itself a fitting choice.

rows.subject: Transformer encoder grid (compute-optimal trajectory)
rows.size_stated: Varied; individual parameter counts not stated for the trajectory.
rows.operation_detail: Derive and show the loss-minimizing N,D allocation under C = np 6ND.

conditions.value: No data repetition; one epoch per configuration

rows.value: N ∝ C^a, D ∝ C^(1−a), L ∝ C^−γ, with a = β/(α+β); fitted γ = 0.15 (0.13, 0.16). No numerical fitted value for a is stated.
rows.uncertainty: 68% bootstrap confidence interval for γ; no interval stated for a
rows.note: The compute-optimal trajectory crosses the minima of the fixed-compute curves in Figure 1. The fitted α and β are reported in R1.
rows.check: V3 concerns the language-model compute-optimal split, so the link to V3 is dropped. The row is a jet-classification result. The allocation exponent can be derived from Table 1: a = β/(α+β) = 0.22/0.66 ≈ 0.33, so N ∝ C^0.33 and D ∝ C^0.67. That is data-heavy, unlike both Kaplan and Hoffmann, which bears on V7. This derived value is not stated in the paper. L ∝ C^-0.15 bears on V5.

rows.subject: Transformer encoder grid (models trained with repeated data)
rows.size_stated: Embedding dimensions varied over {4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 96, 128, 256, 512}; individual parameter counts not stated.
rows.operation_detail: Measure early-stopped validation loss with repeated epochs on fixed training datasets; fit loss versus dataset size above the overfitting threshold.

conditions.value: Fixed dataset sizes from 1k to 1M samples
Repeated data; early-stopped at lowest validation loss

rows.measure: Loss-versus-dataset scaling form and exponent under repetition
rows.baseline: Single-pass large-model comparison described by L∞ + B/D^β
rows.value: L(Drep) = L∞ + Brep/Drep^βrep; βrep is reported as approximately β, with repetition primarily changing Brep. No fitted global βrep value is stated here.
rows.note: The paper reports a smooth power-law scaling in dataset size for early-stopped loss above the overfitting threshold.

source_check.locator_found: Section 3.2, Equation 4, Figure 2 caption and following paragraphs.

rows.subject: Transformer encoder grid (models trained with repeated data)
rows.size_stated: Embedding dimensions varied; individual parameter counts not stated.
rows.operation_detail: Compare early-stopped validation loss and compute under repeated-data training with the no-repetition compute-optimal frontier.

conditions.value: Fixed datasets ranging from D = 1k to D = 1M

rows.measure: Compute required for comparable loss; loss behavior as repeated-data compute increases
rows.value: Repeated-data models lie above the compute-optimal line; roughly a factor of 10 more compute is reported to reach the same loss. Benefits eventually saturate, with validation performance described as saturating or overfitting.
rows.note: The paper describes departures from an indefinitely continuing single-pass compute-optimal power law under fixed-data repetition.
rows.check: Along the above-threshold trajectory the compute exponent is the same (∝ C^0.15) but needs about 10× more compute. At fixed D, loss saturates or overfits, so the curves bend away from the single-pass frontier.

source_check.correct: V5: partial for unrestricted scaling with fixed-data repetition. V7: observed; fixed-dataset compute curves saturate or overfit. Across dataset sizes above the threshold, the repeated-data trajectory retains the compute exponent but requires roughly 10 times more compute.
source_check.locator_found: Section 3.2, Figure 2a–b caption and paragraph following Equation 4.
source_check.problem: The single partial state obscures that departures from a single compute power law support V7.

rows.subject: Transformer encoder models across nine JetClass signal processes
rows.size_stated: Varied; model sizes are shown in Figure 5 but not assigned individually in the text.
rows.operation_detail: Map cross-entropy loss and training dataset size to QCD background rejection at fixed signal efficiencies.

conditions.value: 50% for signal types except H → lνqq′ (99%) and t → blν (99.5%)

rows.measure: QCD background rejection as a function of loss and dataset size
rows.baseline: ParT (plain) trained on the full 100M dataset, shown as a reference
rows.value: The text states the ParT reference is crossed at the 100M-jet scale and that the fitted scaling predicts further improvement in background rejection as dataset size and compute increase; individual rejection values are shown in figures.

relationships.condition: JetClass boosted-jet classification, single-pass training, and early-stopped repeated-data training above the overfitting threshold
relationships.reason: The L(N,D) power-law fit holds across orders of magnitude with α=0.44, β=0.22 and γ=0.15 (R1, R2). Data power laws hold for four input configurations (R6–R9) and under repetition with βrep≈β (R3).
relationships.display_finding: The joint model/data power law held across orders of magnitude with α=0.44, β=0.22 and γ=0.15, while data scaling held across four input configurations and repetition preserved βrep≈β.

tranche.reason: The study tests scaling-law forms using its own supervised boosted-jet classification experiments, extending them to a scientific setting beyond text pretraining.
